questions.question: Which of following silver coins was introduced by Sultan Shamsuddin Iltutmish?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tanka**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Tanka was a silver coin introduced by Sultan Shamsuddin Iltutmish in the Delhi Sultanate.
 
• Iltutmish issued the Tanka in the early 13th century as a part of his currency reforms.
 
• The Tanka weighed about 175 grains (approximately 11 grams) of silver.
 
• This coinage system set the standard for the currency in the Indian subcontinent during the medieval period.
 
• The introduction of the Tanka helped stabilize the economy and facilitated trade within the Sultanate.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Iltutmish:** Shamsuddin Iltutmish was the third ruler of the Mamluk dynasty in Delhi, known for his administrative and military strategies.
 
• **Currency Reforms:** Iltutmish's introduction of the Tanka and Jittal (copper coins) was part of his effort to streamline and standardize the currency system.
 
• **Economic Impact:** The Tanka contributed significantly to the economic development of the Delhi Sultanate by facilitating trade and commerce.
 
• **Historical Significance:** The Tanka remained in use even after the fall of the Delhi Sultanate, influencing the coinage of subsequent dynasties.
 
• **Standardization:** The weight and purity standards set by the Tanka were adhered to by later rulers, ensuring consistency in the monetary system.

questions.question: Wasifuddin Dagar was associated with which of the following classical music genres?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dhrupad**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Wasifuddin Dagar is a prominent exponent of **Dhrupad**, a genre of Hindustani classical music.
 
• Dhrupad is one of the oldest forms of North Indian classical music and has its roots in the chanting of Vedic hymns and mantras.
 
• Wasifuddin Dagar belongs to the Dagar family, which has been an integral part of Dhrupad tradition for 20 generations.
 
• He is known for his deep, meditative, and powerful rendition of Dhrupad, continuing the legacy of the Dagarvani style.
 
• Wasifuddin Dagar has performed in various prestigious music festivals in India and abroad, spreading the essence of Dhrupad.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dhrupad:**

 
 
• Dhrupad is characterized by its austere and spiritual nature, focusing on precise intonation and elaborate improvisation.
 
• It includes an extensive Alap (improvisation without rhythm) followed by a composition set to a specific Tala (rhythmic cycle).
 
 
 
• **Ghazal:**
 
 
• A poetic form consisting of rhyming couplets and a refrain, often expressing the pain of loss and the beauty of love.
 
• Ghazals can be set to music, and are popular in both Hindustani classical and semi-classical genres.
 
 
 
• **Tarana:**
 
 
• A style of vocal music in Hindustani classical music where certain words and syllables are used in a fast rendition, often incorporating rhythmic patterns.
 
• It is characterized by the use of mnemonic syllables, such as "ta", "na", "da", and "re".
 
 
 
• **Khyal:**
 
 
• A major vocal style in Hindustani classical music, known for its flexibility and elaborate improvisation.
 
• Khyal compositions are usually based on a specific Raga and are performed in a slow tempo (Vilambit) followed by a fast tempo (Drut).

questions.question: When was the Lahore declaration signed between India and Pakistan?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__February 1999__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Lahore Declaration was signed between India and Pakistan on **February 21, 1999**.
 
• This agreement aimed to de-escalate tensions between the two countries and promote peace.
 
• Indian Prime Minister **Atal Bihari Vajpayee** and Pakistani Prime Minister **Nawaz Sharif** were the signatories.
 
• The declaration emphasized the need for both countries to resolve their disputes through **bilateral dialogue** and respect for each other’s sovereignty.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Simla Agreement**:

 
 
• The Simla Agreement was signed between India and Pakistan on **July 2, 1972**.
 
• It aimed at ensuring peace and stability in the region post the 1971 war.
 
 
 
• **Indo-Pakistani War of 1947-48**:
 
 
• Also known as the First Kashmir War, it was fought between India and Pakistan over the princely state of Jammu and Kashmir.
 
• The war began in October 1947 and ended in December 1948.
 
 
 
• **Indo-Pakistani War of 1965**:
 
 
• This war was fought between India and Pakistan from April 1965 to September 1965.
 
• The conflict began following Pakistan's Operation Gibraltar, which was designed to infiltrate forces into Jammu and Kashmir to cause insurgency against Indian rule.
 
 
 
• **Kargil War**:
 
 
• The Kargil War took place between May and July 1999 in the Kargil district of Jammu and Kashmir and along the Line of Control (LOC).
 
• It was fought between India and Pakistan as Pakistani soldiers and Kashmiri militants infiltrated into Indian territory.

questions.question: According to Global Multidimensional Poverty Index 2022, what was the population of the poor in India in 2020?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**228.9 million**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• According to the Global Multidimensional Poverty Index 2022, the population of the poor in India in 2020 was **228.9 million**.
 
• The Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) is published by the **United Nations Development Programme (UNDP)** and the **Oxford Poverty and Human Development Initiative (OPHI)**.
 
• The MPI considers multiple deprivations across health, education, and living standards, offering a comprehensive measure of poverty.
 
• India has shown significant progress in reducing multidimensional poverty over the years, but challenges remain in addressing inequalities.
 
• The report highlights the need for targeted policies to address the various dimensions of poverty and improve overall well-being.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI)**:

 
 
• Introduced in 2010, it measures poverty beyond income-based metrics, considering factors like health, education, and living standards.
 
• Each dimension is equally weighted and includes indicators such as nutrition, child mortality, years of schooling, and access to sanitation.
 
 
 
• **Global Trends**:
 
 
• The MPI report provides insights into global poverty trends, highlighting regions and countries that have made significant progress or face major challenges.
 
• Sub-Saharan Africa and South Asia are regions with the highest levels of multidimensional poverty.
 
 
 
• **Policy Implications**:
 
 
• Data from the MPI report are used by policymakers to design and implement effective poverty alleviation programs.
 
• Policies focusing on health, education, and basic living conditions are crucial for addressing multidimensional poverty.
 
 
 
• **Poverty Reduction Strategies**:
 
 
• Strategies like social safety nets, education reforms, and healthcare accessibility are essential in reducing poverty.
 
• Community-driven development and inclusive economic growth also play significant roles in poverty reduction.

questions.question: The part of a temple wherein the main deity of the temple is housed is known as the ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Garbha Griha**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Garbha Griha** is the sanctum sanctorum of a Hindu temple where the main deity is enshrined.
 
• It is typically a small, windowless, and dark chamber located at the center of the temple.
 
• The term **Garbha Griha** literally translates to "womb chamber" in Sanskrit, symbolizing the spiritual core of the temple.
 
• Only priests are allowed to enter the Garbha Griha to perform rituals and offer prayers to the deity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Stupa**: A Buddhist structure containing relics, typically the remains of Buddhist monks or nuns, used as a place of meditation.
 
• **Shikara**: The spire or tower above the Garbha Griha in North Indian temples, symbolizing the mountain peak and representing the divine abode.
 
• **Mandap**: A pillared hall or pavilion in a Hindu temple used for conducting religious rituals and ceremonies.
 
• The **architecture** and layout of Hindu temples are designed to represent the cosmos, with the Garbha Griha being the focal point.
 
• In South Indian temples, the equivalent of a Shikara is known as the **Vimana**.

questions.question: Sama Chakeva is a folk dance based on the mythological story of the siblings Sama and Chakeva, in which the brother goes to an extreme extent to save his sister. With which State of India is this folk dance associated?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bihar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Sama Chakeva** is a traditional folk dance associated with the state of **Bihar**.
 
• This dance is performed during the **Kartik month** of the Hindu calendar, specifically in the Mithila region.
 
• The dance depicts the **mythological story** of the siblings Sama and Chakeva, highlighting the bond between brother and sister.
 
• **Mithila region**, where the dance is most popular, covers parts of Bihar and Nepal.
 
• The dance is performed by women, and it involves singing folk songs and creating clay idols representing the characters of the story.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mithila Painting:** Also known as Madhubani painting, this is a famous art form from the Mithila region of Bihar, characterized by complex geometrical patterns.
 
• **Chhath Puja:** A significant festival in Bihar, dedicated to the Sun God, celebrated with much fervor and involves rigorous rituals.
 
• **Bhojpuri Language:** Widely spoken in Bihar, Bhojpuri is a part of the Bihari languages group and has a rich tradition of folk songs and literature.
 
• **Jat-Jatin Dance:** Another popular folk dance of Bihar, depicting the life of a married couple and their day-to-day struggles.
 
• **Folk Music:** Bihar has a rich tradition of folk music, including genres like Birha, Kajari, and Sohar, often associated with various life events and seasons.

questions.question: The 'Rule of Law' is a key feature of the Indian Constitution which is a doctrine ascribed to ________________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Albert Venn Dicey**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Albert Venn Dicey, a British jurist, is renowned for his work on the concept of the 'Rule of Law' in his book "Introduction to the Study of the Law of the Constitution" published in 1885.
 
• Dicey outlined three main principles of the 'Rule of Law': the supremacy of law, equality before the law, and the predominance of legal spirit.
 
• The 'Rule of Law' doctrine emphasizes that no one is above the law, and all individuals and institutions are subject to and accountable to the law.
 
• Dicey's concept significantly influenced the legal systems of many democratic countries, including India, where the 'Rule of Law' is a fundamental principle enshrined in the Constitution.
 
• His work laid the foundation for the modern understanding of constitutional law and the protection of individual rights against arbitrary governance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Supremacy of Law:** According to Dicey, the law is supreme and no one is above it, including the government itself. This principle is crucial in preventing the abuse of power.
 
• **Equality Before Law:** Dicey emphasized that every person, regardless of status or position, is subject to the same laws and is entitled to the same legal protections.
 
• **Predominance of Legal Spirit:** Dicey argued that the constitution is not the source but the consequence of the rights of individuals as defined and enforced by the courts.
 
• **Indian Constitution and Rule of Law:** The Indian Constitution incorporates the principle of the 'Rule of Law' in its Preamble and the Fundamental Rights, ensuring justice, liberty, and equality to all citizens.
 
• **Judicial Review:** The concept of judicial review in India, which allows the judiciary to review and invalidate laws and actions of the government that violate the Constitution, is derived from Dicey's principles of the 'Rule of Law'.

questions.question: Who among the following Governor Generals of India wrote about the predicament of Indian weavers, “The bones of the cotton weavers are scattered on the plains of India”?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lord William Bentinck**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Lord William Bentinck served as the Governor-General of India from 1828 to 1835.
 
• He is known for his significant social reforms including the abolition of Sati.
 
• Bentinck highlighted the plight of Indian weavers due to British policies that favored British textiles over local products.
 
• His quote, "The bones of the cotton weavers are scattered on the plains of India," reflects the devastating impact of these policies on Indian textile workers.
 
• His tenure is often remembered for addressing the economic and social issues created by British colonial policies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Industrial Revolution Impact:** The British Industrial Revolution led to the import of cheap British textiles, severely impacting Indian weavers.
 
• **Economic Policies:** British economic policies during colonial rule were aimed at benefiting British industries at the expense of Indian economy.
 
• **Sati Abolition:** One of the major social reforms under Bentinck was the abolition of the practice of Sati in 1829.
 
• **Education Reforms:** Bentinck also initiated reforms in the Indian education system, promoting English as the medium of instruction.
 
• **Judicial Reforms:** He made significant changes to the judicial system, including the introduction of jury trials and the appointment of Indians to higher judicial positions.

questions.question: The Dudhsagar waterfall is a major tourist place of _______ State.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Goa**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Dudhsagar Waterfall is located on the Mandovi River in the Indian state of Goa.
 
• It is one of the tallest waterfalls in India, with a height of 310 meters (1017 feet).
 
• Dudhsagar translates to 'Sea of Milk' in Konkani, referencing the white frothy water cascading down the rocks.
 
• The waterfall is a popular tourist attraction, especially during the monsoon season when it is in full flow.
 
• It is situated in the Bhagwan Mahaveer Sanctuary and Mollem National Park, adding to its natural beauty and biodiversity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tourism in Goa:** Goa is known for its stunning beaches, vibrant nightlife, and rich cultural heritage.
 
• **Bhagwan Mahaveer Sanctuary:** This sanctuary is the largest wildlife reserve in Goa, covering an area of 240 square kilometers.
 
• **Western Ghats:** Dudhsagar Waterfall is part of the Western Ghats, a UNESCO World Heritage site and one of the eight "hottest hotspots" of biological diversity in the world.
 
• **Accessibility:** The waterfall is accessible by a short hike or by a jeep safari through the lush forest, adding an element of adventure for visitors.
 
• **Railway View:** The waterfall can also be viewed from a train journey on the Vasco Da Gama – Londa route, providing a picturesque experience for travelers.

questions.question: Who became the first woman to win two gold medals in a single Para Asian Games event in 2023?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sheetal Devi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Sheetal Devi became the first woman to win two gold medals in a single Para Asian Games event in 2023.
 
• She achieved this historic feat in archery at the 4th Asian Para Games held in Hangzhou, China.
 
• Sheetal Devi won gold in both the individual W1 archery event and the mixed team W1 event.
 
• Her performance has been widely celebrated and recognized as a significant achievement in Indian para-sports.
 
• Sheetal's victories are a testament to her dedication and exceptional skill in archery.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Para Asian Games:**

 
 
• The Para Asian Games are a multi-sport event held every four years for athletes with disabilities from all over Asia.
 
• The first Para Asian Games were held in 2010 in Guangzhou, China.
 
• The event includes a wide range of sports, similar to the Asian Games, but adapted for athletes with disabilities.
 
 
 
• **Archery in Para Sports:**
 
 
• Archery is a popular sport in para-sports, with events for athletes with physical disabilities.
 
• The categories in para-archery include recurve, compound, and W1 (wheelchair users with impairments in all four limbs).
 
 
 
• **India's Performance in Para Asian Games:**
 
 
• India has shown impressive performances in the Para Asian Games, securing numerous medals in various sports.
 
• The country has been improving its ranking and medal count with each edition of the games.
 
 
 
• **Support for Para Athletes in India:**
 
 
• The Indian government and various sports organizations provide support and training facilities for para-athletes.
 
• Initiatives like the Target Olympic Podium Scheme (TOPS) offer financial assistance and training support to elite para-athletes.

questions.question: In the periodic table, what is the trend for atomic radius as you move from left to right across a period (horizontal row)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Atomic radius decreases**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• As you move from left to right across a period in the periodic table, atomic radius decreases.
 
• This decrease is due to the increase in nuclear charge (number of protons) which pulls electrons closer to the nucleus.
 
• Despite the addition of more electrons, they are added to the same energy level, resulting in a stronger attraction between the nucleus and the electrons.
 
• The increased effective nuclear charge reduces the size of the electron cloud, thereby decreasing the atomic radius.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Effective Nuclear Charge (Z_eff)**: The net positive charge experienced by an electron in a multi-electron atom, influencing atomic size.
 
• **Shielding Effect**: Electrons in inner shells can shield outer electrons from the full charge of the nucleus, but across a period, the shielding effect does not increase significantly.
 
• **Ionic Radius**: The radius of an atom's ion. Cations (positively charged ions) are smaller than their neutral atoms, while anions (negatively charged ions) are larger.
 
• **Periodic Trends**: Periodic trends are patterns in the periodic table that show the variation in certain properties, such as atomic radius, ionization energy, and electronegativity.
 
• **Atomic Radius Measurement**: Atomic radius is typically measured in picometers (pm) or angstroms (Å), where 1 Å = 100 pm.

questions.question: Gulabo Sapera, a legendry folk dancer from Kalbeliya tribe, Rajasthan, received Padma Shri in the year ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2016**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Gulabo Sapera, a renowned folk dancer from the Kalbeliya tribe in Rajasthan, was honored with the Padma Shri in 2016.
 
• The Padma Shri is the fourth highest civilian award in India, recognizing distinguished contributions in various fields.
 
• Gulabo Sapera is known for popularizing the Kalbeliya dance form internationally.
 
• Kalbeliya dance, associated with the Kalbeliya community, is characterized by its fluid movements and vibrant costumes, often performed to the tunes of traditional Rajasthani music.
 
• The award recognized her efforts in preserving and promoting the rich cultural heritage of Rajasthan.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kalbeliya Dance**

 
 
• Kalbeliya dance is a traditional dance form performed by the Kalbeliya community, also known as snake charmers, in Rajasthan.
 
• It is known for its serpentine dance movements and vibrant, colorful costumes adorned with mirror work.
 
• The dance form is recognized as an intangible cultural heritage by UNESCO.
 
 
 
• **Padma Awards**
 
 
• The Padma Awards are one of the highest civilian honors in India, instituted in 1954.
 
• They are conferred in three categories: Padma Vibhushan, Padma Bhushan, and Padma Shri.
 
• The awards are given in various disciplines such as art, social work, public affairs, science and engineering, trade and industry, medicine, literature and education, sports, and civil service.
 
 
 
• **Gulabo Sapera's Contributions**
 
 
• Gulabo Sapera has performed internationally, taking the Kalbeliya dance to global platforms.
 
• She has also worked towards the upliftment of the Kalbeliya community, promoting education and healthcare.
 
• Her life and achievements have inspired many documentaries and books.
 
 
 
• **UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage**
 
 
• UNESCO's Intangible Cultural Heritage list aims to ensure better protection of important cultural heritages around the world.
 
• The list recognizes traditions or living expressions inherited from our ancestors and passed on to our descendants, such as oral traditions, performing arts, social practices, rituals, festive events, and knowledge and practices concerning nature and the universe.

questions.question: Which of the following white papers, released by NITI Aayog, is related to Public Health Surveillance in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Vision 2035**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Vision 2035** is a white paper released by NITI Aayog focusing on the future of **Public Health Surveillance (PHS) in India**.
 
• The document outlines a strategy for **strengthening public health surveillance** systems to improve disease detection, monitoring, and response.
 
• It emphasizes the need for **integrated health information platforms** for real-time data sharing among healthcare providers and policymakers.
 
• The white paper envisions a shift from **reactive to proactive surveillance**, leveraging technology and data analytics.
 
• It aims to establish a robust public health surveillance system by **2035** to enhance India's capacity to prevent, detect, and respond to health emergencies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Public Health Surveillance:**

 
 
• It is the continuous, systematic collection, analysis, and interpretation of health-related data needed for planning, implementation, and evaluation of public health practice.
 
• Surveillance provides essential information for the control and prevention of disease outbreaks.
 
 
 
• **Integrated Health Information Platform (IHIP):**
 
 
• An advanced information technology platform for disease surveillance in India.
 
• It aims to provide real-time data for early detection and management of disease outbreaks.
 
 
 
• **National Centre for Disease Control (NCDC):**
 
 
• A central organization responsible for monitoring and controlling disease outbreaks in India.
 
• It provides technical assistance to the states and union territories in the field of disease surveillance.
 
 
 
• **Digital Health Mission:**
 
 
• An initiative to create a digital health ecosystem in India.
 
• It includes the creation of a unique health ID for every citizen, digitization of health records, and development of registries for healthcare providers and facilities.
 
 
 
• **One Health Approach:**
 
 
• A collaborative effort of multiple disciplines working locally, nationally, and globally to achieve optimal health outcomes by recognizing the interconnection between people, animals, plants, and their shared environment.
 
• It is crucial for improving public health surveillance and combating zoonotic diseases.

questions.question: Who amongst the following said that the government fiscal policy should be used to stabilise the level of output and employment?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**JM Keynes**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• John Maynard Keynes was a British economist whose ideas fundamentally changed the theory and practice of macroeconomics and the economic policies of governments.
 
• Keynes advocated for increased government expenditures and lower taxes to stimulate demand and pull the global economy out of the Depression.
 
• His most important work, "The General Theory of Employment, Interest, and Money" (1936), argued that aggregate demand determines overall economic activity and that inadequate aggregate demand can lead to prolonged periods of high unemployment.
 
• Keynesian economics focuses on using active government policy to manage economic cycles and is considered a demand-side theory that focuses on changes in the economy over the short run.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fiscal Policy:** Government adjusts its spending levels and tax rates to monitor and influence a nation's economy. It is used to achieve macroeconomic objectives such as growth, employment, and inflation control.
 
• **Aggregate Demand:** The total demand for goods and services within a particular market. Keynesian economics suggests that aggregate demand is influenced by public and private economic decisions.
 
• **Great Depression:** A severe worldwide economic depression that took place mostly during the 1930s, originating in the United States. Keynes's theories were developed in response to the economic difficulties of this period.
 
• **Multiplier Effect:** An economic term referring to the phenomenon where an initial injection of spending (usually by the government) leads to increased consumption and hence results in a greater final increase in national income.
 
• **Keynesian Revolution:** Refers to the widespread acceptance during the mid-20th century of Keynes's ideas about how governments should intervene in the economy to manage demand and prevent prolonged recessions.

questions.question: Which of the following options is an example of a decomposer in an ecosystem?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Fungus**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Fungi** are organisms that break down dead organic material, making them essential decomposers in ecosystems.
 
• They release **enzymes** to decompose complex organic substances into simpler compounds.
 
• Fungi play a critical role in nutrient cycling by **releasing nutrients** back into the soil for plant use.
 
• They exist in various forms, including **mushrooms, molds, and yeasts**.
 
• Fungi can decompose a wide range of substances, including **wood, leaves, and animal remains**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Decomposers**: Organisms that break down dead or decaying organisms, and in doing so, carry out the natural process of decomposition.
 
• **Bacteria**: Along with fungi, bacteria are also primary decomposers in ecosystems, breaking down organic material at a microscopic level.
 
• **Detritivores**: These are organisms like earthworms and certain insects that consume detritus (decomposing organic matter) and contribute to decomposition.
 
• **Nutrient Cycling**: The process by which decomposers release nutrients back into the environment, making them available for primary producers like plants.
 
• **Symbiotic Relationships**: Some fungi form symbiotic associations with plant roots (mycorrhizae), aiding in nutrient absorption for the plant while receiving carbohydrates in return.

questions.concept: Socio - Religious Reform Movements in the 19th and 20th CE India
questions.question: Who among the following social reformers wrote Brahmo Covenant which was a statement of the creed of the Brahmo Samaj?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Debendranath Tagore**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Debendranath Tagore** was a prominent leader of the Brahmo Samaj and a key figure in the Bengal Renaissance.
 
• He authored the **Brahmo Covenant**, which is a statement of the creed of the Brahmo Samaj.
 
• Debendranath Tagore was instrumental in the development and propagation of **Brahmoism**, a reformist movement within Hinduism.
 
• He was the father of Rabindranath Tagore, the renowned poet and Nobel laureate.
 
• His contributions significantly shaped the religious and social reform movements in 19th century India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Brahmo Samaj**:

 
 
• Founded by Raja Ram Mohan Roy in 1828, it aimed at reforming the social and religious practices of Hindu society.
 
• The Brahmo Samaj advocated for monotheism and rejected the caste system and idol worship.
 
 
 
• **Keshab Chandra Sen**:
 
 
• He was a prominent Indian social reformer who joined the Brahmo Samaj in 1857.
 
• Sen later founded his own sect, the Brahmo Samaj of India, in 1866.
 
 
 
• **Raja Ram Mohan Roy**:
 
 
• He is considered the father of the Indian Renaissance and was the founder of the Brahmo Samaj.
 
• Roy campaigned against social evils like Sati and child marriage.
 
 
 
• **Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar**:
 
 
• He was a key figure in the Bengal Renaissance and worked for the upliftment of women and education reforms.
 
• Vidyasagar played a significant role in the Widow Remarriage Act of 1856.

questions.question: In which of the following states is the famous International Sand Art Festival organised, where artists get enthralled by the diverse thoughts and their elucidation on sand?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Odisha**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The International Sand Art Festival is held annually at Chandrabhaga Beach, near Konark in Odisha.
 
• This festival attracts renowned sand artists from India and around the world to showcase their skills.
 
• The event is organized by the Odisha Tourism Department, promoting the state's rich cultural heritage.
 
• It usually takes place in December, coinciding with the Konark Festival, which celebrates classical dance forms.
 
• The festival includes various themes each year, ranging from culture, heritage, to global issues like climate change.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chandrabhaga Beach**

 
 
• Located 3 km from the Sun Temple of Konark, it is one of the most famous beaches in Odisha.
 
• Known for its serene environment and cultural importance.
 
 
 
• **Sand Art**
 
 
• A form of art that involves shaping and sculpting sand into various forms and structures.
 
• It is temporary and often created in public spaces like beaches.
 
 
 
• **Konark Festival**
 
 
• Held every year from December 1 to 5 in Konark, Odisha.
 
• Features classical dance performances against the backdrop of the Sun Temple.
 
 
 
• **Odisha Tourism**
 
 
• Actively promotes the state's cultural and natural heritage through various festivals and events.
 
• Focuses on sustainable and responsible tourism practices.

questions.question: Which sector uses the groundwater maximally?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Agriculture**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Agriculture is the largest consumer of groundwater globally, accounting for approximately 70% of all groundwater withdrawals.
 
• In countries like India, agriculture consumes about 90% of the extracted groundwater.
 
• Groundwater is crucial for irrigation, especially in arid and semi-arid regions where surface water is insufficient.
 
• Over-extraction of groundwater for agricultural purposes has led to significant depletion of aquifers in many regions.
 
• Efficient water management practices in agriculture are essential to ensure the sustainability of groundwater resources.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Groundwater Depletion:** Overuse of groundwater for agricultural purposes can lead to falling water tables and the drying up of wells.
 
• **Irrigation Techniques:** Drip and sprinkler irrigation are more water-efficient methods compared to traditional flood irrigation.
 
• **Water Conservation:** Techniques such as rainwater harvesting and the use of drought-resistant crops can help in conserving groundwater.
 
• **Government Policies:** Many governments have implemented policies to regulate groundwater extraction and promote sustainable agricultural practices.
 
• **Climate Change:** Changes in climate patterns can affect the availability and demand for groundwater in agriculture.

questions.question: The black coating formed on silver jewellery is:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ag2S**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The black coating formed on silver jewellery is primarily due to the formation of silver sulfide (Ag2S).
 
• Silver reacts with hydrogen sulfide (H2S) present in the air, leading to the formation of Ag2S, which appears black.
 
• This reaction is a common example of tarnishing, which is a surface phenomenon affecting metals like silver.
 
• Ag2S is a compound consisting of two silver atoms and one sulfur atom.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tarnishing**: Tarnishing is the process where a metal surface loses its luster due to a chemical reaction, often forming a thin layer of corrosion.
 
• **Hydrogen Sulfide (H2S)**: H2S is a colorless gas with the characteristic foul odor of rotten eggs; it is often present in the environment in small amounts.
 
• **Prevention**: To prevent tarnishing, silver jewellery can be stored in airtight containers or treated with anti-tarnish coatings.
 
• **Cleaning**: Tarnished silver can be cleaned using various methods, including chemical dips, polishing cloths, or mild abrasives.
 
• **Oxidation**: While tarnishing involves the formation of a sulfide layer, oxidation refers to a broader category of reactions where a material loses electrons, often involving oxygen.

questions.question: The Megalithic site ________ is a site on the river Ghod, a tributary of the Bhima.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Inamgaon**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Inamgaon is an important archaeological site located on the banks of the river Ghod, which is a tributary of the Bhima River in Maharashtra, India.
 
• The site dates back to the Chalcolithic (Copper Age) period, approximately between 1600 BCE and 700 BCE.
 
• Excavations at Inamgaon have revealed evidence of early farming communities, including the cultivation of crops such as barley, wheat, and legumes.
 
• Artifacts found at the site include pottery, tools, and ornaments, providing insights into the daily life and culture of the people who lived there.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Megalithic Culture:** Refers to a prehistoric period characterized by the construction of large stone structures or monuments, such as dolmens and menhirs.
 
• **Chalcolithic Period:** Also known as the Copper Age, this period marks the transition between the Neolithic (Stone Age) and the Bronze Age, characterized by the use of copper tools.
 
• **Excavation Techniques:** Archaeological excavations at sites like Inamgaon involve systematic digging and recording of artifacts to understand past human activities and cultures.
 
• **Ghod River:** A significant river in Maharashtra, India, it is a tributary of the Bhima River, which is part of the larger Krishna River basin.
 
• **Bhima River:** One of the major rivers in southern India, it flows through the states of Maharashtra and Karnataka and is a tributary of the Krishna River.

questions.question: Which of the following crops takes almost a year to grow?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sugarcane**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Sugarcane is a tropical and subtropical crop, grown in a warm climate with abundant water supply.
 
• The crop cycle for sugarcane varies from 10 to 18 months, depending on the variety and growing conditions.
 
• In India, sugarcane planting typically begins in February to April and harvesting starts from November to March of the following year.
 
• This crop requires a long growing period to accumulate high sugar content in the stalks, making it a year-long cultivation.
 
• Sugarcane is primarily grown in states like Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, and Andhra Pradesh.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ratoon Cropping:** Sugarcane can be ratooned, meaning the regrowth from the stubbles of the harvested crop can be used for the next planting.
 
• **Water Requirements:** The crop requires about 1500-2500 mm of water throughout its growing period, which is why irrigation plays a crucial role in sugarcane farming.
 
• **Soil Type:** Sugarcane thrives in well-drained loamy soil with a pH range of 6.5 to 7.5, though it can grow in a variety of soils.
 
• **Economic Importance:** Sugarcane is a major source of sugar and ethanol production, contributing significantly to the agricultural economy in many countries.
 
• **By-products:** Bagasse, a by-product of sugarcane, is used in the production of paper, and as a biofuel for electricity generation in sugar mills.

questions.question: The strength of Supreme Court has increased to how many judges as of 13 Feb 2023?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**34**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The strength of the Supreme Court of India has been increased to **34 judges** as of 13 February 2023.
 
• This includes the Chief Justice of India (CJI) and 33 other judges.
 
• The increase in the number of judges aims to reduce the pendency of cases and expedite the delivery of justice.
 
• The last increase in the number of judges was approved by the President of India in August 2019, from 31 to 34.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Judicial Appointments**: Judges of the Supreme Court are appointed by the President of India under Article 124(2) of the Constitution.
 
• **Collegium System**: The appointment of judges follows the collegium system, where the Chief Justice of India and a forum of four senior-most judges recommend the appointments.
 
• **Retirement Age**: The retirement age for Supreme Court judges in India is 65 years.
 
• **Jurisdiction**: The Supreme Court has original, appellate, and advisory jurisdiction, making it the highest judicial authority in India.
 
• **Pendency of Cases**: As of 2023, the Supreme Court faces a significant backlog of cases, making the increase in the number of judges crucial for faster resolution.

questions.question: The legislative powers in India are divided into three lists, which are the Union List, the State List and the __________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Concurrent List**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Concurrent List includes subjects of common interest to both the Union and State governments.
 
• It is enumerated in the Seventh Schedule of the Indian Constitution.
 
• Both the Parliament and State Legislatures can make laws on the subjects in the Concurrent List.
 
• In case of conflict between the Union and State laws on a Concurrent List subject, the Union law prevails.
 
• Examples of subjects in the Concurrent List include criminal law, marriage and divorce, bankruptcy and insolvency, and education.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Union List:** Contains subjects of national importance like defense, foreign affairs, atomic energy, and railways. Only the Parliament can legislate on these subjects.
 
• **State List:** Contains subjects of local or state importance like police, public health, agriculture, and fisheries. Only the State Legislatures can legislate on these subjects.
 
• **Federal Structure:** India follows a quasi-federal structure, where powers are divided between the central and state governments, with a strong centralizing bias.
 
• **Seventh Schedule:** The division of powers between the Union and State governments is outlined in the Seventh Schedule of the Indian Constitution, which contains the Union List, State List, and Concurrent List.
 
• **Residual Powers:** Any subject not mentioned in any of the three lists falls under the residuary powers, which are vested in the Parliament.
